items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: Interviewer mentions Louis Armstrong as a reference point for a date ('Louis Armstrong came down') and a rumor ('he said he was a pallbearer'), but the interviewee (Earl Humphrey) does not claim to have met, played with, or known Louis Armstrong personally, only responding to the interviewer's narra

ctx.x: Oh, he didn't hear anything about it until I come back in 1941.

Really? Didn't he? You didn't hear anything about it? No. Because, you see, he is supposed to have died on July 4th, 1931, which would be two or three months after you left. Now, I don't know whether that date's right, but the reason why they say that is because that's supposed to be the year Louis Armstrong came down. Yeah. He said he was a pallbearer. Right. That's what they said.
Well, you see, I wasn't here. I couldn't give you no direct date on that.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Well, Louis' room, A.M. sits right around the corner. Said, man, we got an opportunity to make some records... We were stuck together. No too much rehearsal.

ctx.x: You hadn't played for six weeks?

That's right. I used to get in them snubs, you know. Used to be a fellow on Fred and 8. Well, you know, tell the truth about it. We'd handle liquor. At speakeasy times. So Rouse found out where he connected with Willie, and Willie told him just about where I stayed at. And Rouse come out and see Rouse. That's piano player. They come out there, I was sitting down in the corner. Well, Louis' room, A.M. sits right around the corner. Said, man, we got an opportunity to make some records. What's it gonna get together?…
I was just mowing there. Excuse me, I'll turn it off in a second.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: Louis put that name right here. ... And Louis being such a good monopolist. Louis, too, man, he was a great guy.

ctx.x: What were you saying about the Ann Cook record? I didn't get that, you know. About her phrasing and stuff?

Yeah, we had to work with her, you know. Get out on time and phrasing the blues, you know, on time. Oh, yeah. I had to work with her for a while, see. Mm-hmm. And Louis being such a good monopolist. Louis, too, man, he was a great guy. He knew how to handle anything. And he'd get in front of her and tell her when to stop and breathe. Pull her right in on it, you know, next phrase.
